subject: other-disciplines
audience: FE Other Disciplines candidates and engineering students
title: The Source That Fell to 30, Not 60
featured_title: THE SOURCE THAT FELL TO 30 NOT 60

presentation.challenge: Eighteen hours represented three half-lives, not two. A 240-unit rate therefore fell to 30, not 60.

practice.primary_question: How is a radioactive activity or exposure-rate quantity calculated after multiple half-lives?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Counting the number of elapsed half-lives incorrectly or subtracting a fixed amount instead of repeatedly halving the quantity.

case_dna.target_misconception: An 18-hour interval with a 6-hour half-life contains only two half-lives, leaving 25% of the initial quantity.
case_dna.why_plausible: The first and last clock readings can be mistaken for two intervals instead of dividing total elapsed time by the half-life.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: 18/6=3 half-lives. The remaining fraction is (1/2)^3=1/8=12.5%, so 240 becomes 30.
case_dna.corrected_model: Use A=A0(1/2)^(t/t1/2), where the exponent is the number of elapsed half-lives.

problem_statement: A radioactive source has an initial measured rate of 240 arbitrary exposure-rate units. Its half-life is 6.0 hours. A note states that after 18 hours only two half-lives have elapsed and reports 60 units remaining. Determine the correct remaining rate after 18 hours and the time required for the rate to fall below 10 units.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The decay law was correct. The half-life count was not.
gates.prompt: How many half-lives occur in 18 hours?

options.label: Use A=A0(1/2)^(t/t_half)
options.reason: Each elapsed half-life halves the remaining quantity.

options.label: Subtract half of A0 every 6 hours
options.reason: Radioactive decay is exponential; each halving applies to the remaining quantity.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Step through the half-lives
gates.result: The rate after 18 hours is 30 units.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the remaining rate
gates.hint: The exponent is the number of half-lives.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the decay note
report: C2. The elapsed time is 18 hours.
C3. Only two half-lives have elapsed, so 60 units remain.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated elapsed time.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: 18 hours contains three 6-hour half-lives, not two.

evidence_choices.label: 18/6=3 and 240(1/2)^3=30
evidence_choices.reason: This directly applies the half-life decay relation.

correction.template: After 18 hours, the measured rate is {remaining} units.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Determine when the rate falls below 10 units

options.label: After exactly 24 hours
options.reason: After 24 h, four half-lives leave 15 units.

options.label: Only after 30 hours
options.reason: The threshold is crossed earlier, at about 27.5 h.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the same decay law
gates.prompt: A quantity starts at 160 units with a 4-hour half-life. What remains after 12 hours?

options.label: 40 units
options.reason: That corresponds to only two half-lives.

gates.explanation: Count elapsed half-lives, then halve the remaining quantity once per half-life.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the half-life calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that radioactive decay follows repeated halving based on the number of elapsed half-lives.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The elapsed-time interval was divided into the wrong number of half-lives.

seo.seo_title: Radioactive Half-Life Decay Calculation | FE Other Disciplines E-092
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Other Disciplines Case E-092: 240 units with a 6-hour half-life falls to 30 units after 18 hours, not 60.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE radioactive half life decay calculation
seo.excerpt: Half-life problems depend on the number of elapsed half-lives. Repeated halving must be applied to the remaining quantity.
seo.direct_answer: With A0=240, half-life 6 h, and t=18 h, three half-lives elapse. A=240(1/2)^3=30 units. The rate falls below 10 units after about 27.5 hours.
